hook_text: 3 rotis, 4 hungry children. How much does each child get? No calculator, just a knife.
clip_script: Family gathering in Gqeberha. 3 rotis, 4 children. Not enough for one each. So cut every roti into quarters: 12 quarters. Share them: 3 quarters each. 3 divided by 4 is three quarters. The fraction is the sharing! Top: what you share. Bottom: how many share. Now 20 sweets, and three quarters are red. Split 20 into 4 groups: 5 each. Three groups: 15 red sweets. Divide by the bottom, times by the top. And 7 rotis between 2? 3 each, 1 left, cut it in half: 3 and a half each. Just never cut the children.
visual_style: Whiteboard rotis being cut into quarters and dealt to four plates; 20 sweets arranged in 4 rows with 3 rows circled.
pacing: The sharing puzzle, the quarters dealt out, the sweets rule, then the leftover roti.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and share 5 oranges between 2 friends in pictures.
